evidence.text: Tjuyu( sometimes transliterated as Thuya or Thuyu) was an Egyptian noblewoman and the mother of queen Tiye, and the wife of Yuya.

evidence.title: Birger Brosa
evidence.text: Birger Brosa (Old Norse: "Birgir Brósa" where "Brósa" means "smiling"), jarl of Sweden 1174–1202, d. 9 January 1202 on Visingsö, was a son of Bengt Snivil and a member of the powerful House of Bjälbo.

evidence.title: Birger Brosa
evidence.text: In the medieval texts he is either called the "jarl of the Swedes" or the "jarl of the Swedes and the Geats".

evidence.title: Birger Brosa
evidence.text: Birger was appointed to the position of jarl during the reign of Knut Eriksson.

evidence.title: Birger Brosa
evidence.text: He maintained the position during Knut's successor Sverker II until his death in 1202.

evidence.title: Birger Brosa
evidence.text: Before 1170, Birger was married to Brigida Haraldsdotter, the daughter of the Norwegian king Harald Gille.

evidence.title: Birger Brosa
evidence.text: She had formerly been married to the Danish pretender Magnus Henriksson, who had briefly ruled in Uppsala 1160–1161.

evidence.title: Birger Brosa
evidence.text: Birger appears to have maintained peace in Sweden during the civil wars that ravaged Denmark and Norway.

evidence.title: Birger Brosa
evidence.text: Many of the pretenders in these kingdoms sought refuge with Birger.

evidence.title: Birger Brosa
evidence.text: Among them were the Birkebeiner chieftains Eystein Meyla and Sverre Sigurdsson who were kinsmen of Brigida Haraldsdotter.

evidence.title: Birger Brosa
evidence.text: Birger's son Philippus was in the service of King Sverre and died as his Earl in 1200.

evidence.title: Birger Brosa
evidence.text: Birger owned estates in Östergötland, Närke, Värmland and Södermanland.

evidence.title: Birger Brosa
evidence.text: He was a great donor to the convent of Riseberga in Närke, where Birgitta spent her last years after Birger's death.

evidence.title: Birger Brosa
evidence.text: As soon as he was dead, a civil war broke out.

evidence.title: Kaoru Hatoyama
evidence.text: After the elections of 2009, she became more widely known as the grandmother of Prime Minister Yukio Hatoyama and his politician brother Kunio Hatoyama.

evidence.title: Hubba bint Hulail
evidence.text: Hubba bint Hulail was the grandmother of Hashim ibn' Abd Manaf, thus the great- great- great- grandmother of the Islamic" Nabī"( Prophet) Muhammad ibn Abdullah.

evidence.title: Mona Hopton Bell
evidence.text: Mona Hopton Bell( 1867- 1940) was a British artist, best known for her portraits of civic figures.

evidence.title: Mona Hopton Bell

evidence.title: Folke Filbyter
evidence.text: Folke Filbyter is the popularized name of the pagan progenitor of the House of Bjelbo clan.

evidence.title: Folke Filbyter
evidence.text: Since Folke is said to have been the great- great- grandfather of Birger Brosa, he would have lived in the 11th century.

evidence.title: Folke Filbyter
evidence.text: His cognomen" Filbyter" is believed to mean" foal biter" and refers to a man who castrates colts with his teeth.

evidence.text: Gülbahar Hatun( 1432 – 1492) was the consort of Sultan Mehmed II, and mother of Sultan Bayezid II of the Ottoman Empire and the grandmother of Selim I.

evidence.title: Bengt Snivil
evidence.text: Bengt Snivil (also known as "Bengt Snivel") from the House of Bjelbo was a Swedish magnate in mid-12th century.
